recipes.name: Prosciutto-Wrapped Cherry-Stuffed Chicken Breasts
ingredients_raw: 2 (6 ounce) skinless, boneless chicken breast halves

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees F (200 degrees C). Brush the inside of an ovenproof skillet with vegetable oil. Set aside.
Mix together cherries, bread crumbs, egg yolk, olive oil, garlic, Parmigiano-Reggiano cheese, thyme, oregano, salt, black pepper, and cayenne pepper in a large bowl until stuffing is combined.
Cut a 1-inch slit in each chicken breast by slicing at an angle from the thick end of the breast toward the thinner end.

Open flap and place one butterflied chicken breast between 2 sheets of heavy plastic (resealable freezer bags work well, too) on a solid, level surface. Firmly pound chicken with the smooth side of a meat mallet to a thickness of 1/2 inch. Repeat with the other breast.
Place each breast on a piece of plastic wrap, divide stuffing evenly between each breast, and roll into a tight roll, twisting the ends of the plastic wrap to create a tight package.

On a piece of plastic wrap, slightly overlap 2 slices prosciutto so they are as wide as the rolled chicken breast. Unwrap rolled chicken breast and place breast at one end of prosciutto. Roll prosciutto around stuffed breast using the plastic to make a tight roll. Repeat with second stuffed breast and remaining 2 slices prosciutto.
Lay 4 pieces of string on a cutting board, about 1-inch apart. Place a chicken roll across the strings and tie each into a knot to keep chicken from unrolling. Repeat with second stuffed breast.

Place stuffed, rolled chicken breasts in the prepared skillet and bake in the preheated oven until prosciutto is browned and crispy and chicken is no longer pink, about 25 minutes. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 165 degrees F (74 degrees C). Remove chicken to a plate and loosely cover with aluminum foil.

Drain grease from the skillet as desired, leaving juice and browned bits. Pour in chicken broth and balsamic vinegar; bring to a boil. Cook, scraping the browned bits from the bottom of the pan, until liquid is reduced by half, 5 to 6 minutes. Remove from heat, add butter, and stir until melted. Season with salt and black pepper.
Remove the twine from chicken; slice into bite-sized pieces. Serve drizzled with sauce.

raw_recipe.headline: Prosciutto-Wrapped Cherry-Stuffed Chicken Breasts
raw_recipe.description: This prosciutto chicken dish features breasts stuffed with herby cheese and dried cherries, wrapped in Italian ham, and served with a balsamic pan sauce.

review.reviewBody: Very, very good. What I like most about this 'company worthy' dish is that it can be prepped entirely ahead of time, cooked to order and looks fabulous. BUT it really very easy. As written this feeds more than 2 - more like 3 or 4. Enjoy this great recipe.

Really delicious. I used a pack of dried cranberries with walnuts (sold as a salad topping actually) instead of cherries and also added a few small dollops of Aloutte garlic and herb cheese spread to the stuffing mixture ((sold in small tubs near the deli at the grocery store). Cooked the chicken in the oven in my cast iron pans. It was SOOOO good. Attached is a before cooked picture.

I tried the Prosciutto-Wrapped Cherry-Stuffed Chicken Breasts for two last night for the first time, and it was terrific. We'll have it again at Valentines dinner with another guest. I added a second egg yolk to make the stuffing more moist and I plan to chop the cherries a bit to distribute the cherries' sweetness more evenly. Lots of fun to create this dish.- Arjay

It is a wonderful recipe and the video made it that much easier to make. Very clever using cling wrap to keep the chicken roll in place while prepping other things. I substituted fresh mango for the dried cherries and it added a lively burst of taste to an already amazing stuffing made velvety by the egg yoke. It's truly scrumptious.

This is a great recipe! I recommend this for everyone. I had to use cranberries instead of cherries and it still tasted amazing. I would recommend at least doubling the filing because mine did not seem to have enough filing for my taste.

WOW! This was so amazing that I am bummed I did not make more. It is the perfect size for 1 or 2 people and tastes so delicious. I made it with another www.allrecipes.com http://allrecipes.com/recipe/9377/roasted-vegetables/

The only change I made was that I did not tie it with string and I used dried spices instead of fresh because that is what I had on hand. It came out amazing and I will make this again and again.

I made this dish and it was delicious! My husband loved it. I have to say it does take some skill to get these ingredients to roll up. The video was very helpful. I tweaked the recipe a little because my husband doesn't like fruit in his stuffing. I used some prepared stuffing and crumbled Italian sausage because that's what I had around the house. I found it hard to wrap the prosciutto around the chicken. I think the deli sliced it too thin and I didn't buy the expensive stuff. When I went to slice the rolls they kind of fell apart. I would definitely sear the roll-ups on both sides before baking them. The video shows this but I don't think the recipe mentions it.

I've made this two different ways and my family loved it each time. The first time I made as instructed with the exception of using cherry flavored cranberries. It was really good. I then made it using a boneless turkey breast and subbing apricots and beef bacon. The turkey was so moist and flavorful. I have a love/hate relationship with balsamic vinegar so I only used half the amount and it was awesome. I served it with whole wax beans and scalloped oysters. Thanks Chef John!

I always seem to overcook and dry out boneless skinless chicken breast. So I was on the lookout for a recipe that would help keep the chicken moist and tender. This is one of the best I’ve found. I did not have cherries so I used cranberries and also replaced the prosciutto with uncured thick cut bacon that I had on hand. I added my favorite herbs and spices. My husband and I agreed it was delicious and definitely company worthy. Reduction of sauce took a while but did happen. Be patient. Enjoy!

Used Italian cherries, "Ciliegie di'Vignola", drained, for the stuffing. I did add some pieces of cherries to the sauce. Couldn't help myself. Served w/haricot green beans & rice pilaf (see Chef John's Classic Rice Pilaf). I plated the rice pilaf in ramekins to mould and inverted it on the plates, garnished with sliced green onions. His stuffing can be used for beef or pork as well. I have also used his stuffing in my seitan. Thank you Chef John!

Really easy to pull off. Substituted dried cranberries instead of cherries. Needed to cook longer than 25 minutes in my oven, and ended up broiling it for a few minutes afterwards. The pieces that were broiled well, had a much more distinct taste, and the prosciutto was much more palatable. Will definitely try this again. Very easy, displays beautifully, and has great potential for customizing to your own palate. Thanks a million for sharing this recipe.
We used fresh cherries and Italian bread because its what we had. Great recipe
I made this for dinner tonight - absolutely delicious and definitely company-worthy! Great recipe and easy-to-follow directions. Thanks!
Surprisingly delicious!
Very good! I made it as described and it turned out great! Be sure to use high quality ingredents.
No changes, unexpected and delicious.
I followed the recipe exactly and it turned out moist and juicy. The cherries were a fun flavor addition. Great special occasion dish.
I made as the recipe called for but if I make it again I will add more stuffing. it lacked a little flavor I thought but I had very large chicken breasts
This received my husbands highest mark of “restaurant quality”!

no changes and it came out Excellent !!
(minus me burning hand on hot pan out of over)
